hints: Focus on what it means that solid CO2 is like solid iodine, think about how the molecules pack together in the solid.
Remember that CO2 forms discrete O=C=O molecules with double bonds, while SiO2 forms a continuous giant network of single Si-O bonds.
Compare their melting points and structures to decide which type of lattice each one has, molecular versus giant covalent.
walkthrough:
**Understand the clue about solid CO2**

Solid iodine is a simple molecular solid. The $\text{I}_2$ molecules sit in regular positions in a lattice, held together by weak London forces.

Since solid $\text{CO}_2$ is similar, it is also a molecular lattice of discrete $\text{CO}_2$ molecules:
$$\text{CO}_2(s) = \text{lattice of O=C=O molecules}$$

**Recall the structure of solid SiO2**

Silicon dioxide is very different. It does not exist as discrete $\text{SiO}_2$ molecules. Each Si is singly bonded to four O atoms in a giant covalent network.

$$\text{Si-O-Si-O network, giant covalent lattice}$$

**Compare and choose**

Both solids have their particles arranged in a regular repeating lattice, but the lattice type is different. One is a simple molecular lattice, the other is a giant covalent lattice.

So the only statement true for both is that they exist in a lattice structure.

options.A: Correct. Both have an ordered lattice. Solid CO2 has a simple molecular lattice with CO2 molecules held by weak intermolecular forces, and solid SiO2 has a giant covalent lattice of Si and O atoms. Lattice just means regular repeating arrangement.
options.B: Incorrect. Only solid CO2 is simple molecular. Solid SiO2 is giant covalent with no discrete molecules, so it needs very high temperature to melt, not weak forces like CO2.
options.C: Incorrect. Only SiO2 has all single covalent bonds (Si-O). CO2 contains double covalent bonds, O=C=O. Students who forget the C=O double bond often pick this trap.
options.D: Incorrect. Only solid CO2 sublimes readily to gas at s.t.p. (dry ice). SiO2 (quartz, sand) has a very high melting point due to strong covalent bonds throughout the giant structure and stays solid.
